entries.06154eaea832e0f8: At the top are [[industry:finance|Finance]] (¥7.654 million), followed by energy, semiconductors, and pharmaceuticals. At the bottom are staffing services and [[industry:retail|Retail]] (¥5.407 million), and the difference from the top industry was 1.42 times. Industries with a high proportion of professionals come out on top, while industries with many store and frontline employees come out at the bottom.

entries.5ed73125d148d854: The "Status of Employees" section of the annual securities report prints the average annual salary of the filing company (non-consolidated). Of the 3,132 companies listed, 3,092 reported this amount, and the overall median was ¥6.64 million. This feature arranges the medians by industry for industries with 10 or more companies covered. All amounts are exactly as printed in the reports, and the only calculated values are the medians and ratios.

entries.f0931cd0ef84ed8d: Each company's amount is exactly as printed for average annual salary (filing company) in the "Status of Employees" section of its annual securities report. The medians and their calculation are calculated values. Industries with fewer than 10 companies covered are not included.
entries.f8b19e57bd43eea5: These amounts are averages for the company that filed the report on a non-consolidated basis, not for the consolidated group as a whole. For holding companies, the amount may appear high because non-consolidated employees are limited to management and professionals. Conversely, for companies that directly employ store or plant employees on a non-consolidated basis, the composition of the frontline workforce is reflected directly in the average. Even when comparing industry medians, care is needed because differences in forms of employment are mixed in.
